articleTitle: Deploying Jenkins, Ansible and Kubernetes to Automate Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment Pipeline
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: A pipeline is set up to build code, run tests, and securely deploy a newer version of the application. Manual errors are minimized or can be eliminated through automated pipelines thus providing developers with standardized feedback loops and facilitating rapid product iteration. This article introduces the entire automated CI/CD channel by deploying Jenkins, Ansible and Kubernetes cluster to host the updated version. The proposed approach provides an easy to implement automation methodology with high scalability and resiliency. The study aims to provide an approach for continuous integration (CI), continuous testing, and continuous delivery (CD) for automating compilation of source code, analysis, testing, deployment, and reports using build pipeline model.

articleTitle: Detection of Road Potholes Using Deep Learning Based Improved YOLOv4 Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: In our daily lives, when we want to connect with the outside world, we use roads as a connecting method between various locations. Road maintenance is a very important task to keep them safe. Potholes on roads may intensify the number of accidents, so detecting potholes and enlightening the concerned department can save the roads from getting worse. The traditional manual detection method was a time-consuming and laborious task. So In this paper, we have trained and tested different deep neural network-based models to detect the presence of potholes on roads. We have taken publicly available dataset from Kaggle and then potholes in road images are identified using object identification algorithms. Deep learning models for one-stage object detection that can be configured in a number of ways, including YOLOv4-CSPDarknet53, YOLOv5s, and modified YOLOv4-CSPDarknet 53 are used to compare their performance in detecting potholes. Performance is compared using Average precision, Average recall, mAP@50%, and inference time. The results showed that the modified YOLOv4 architecture outperformed compared with the other deep learning models with the highest Average precision (0.84), Average recall (0.79), F1 - Score (0.81), and mAP@50% (0.82).

articleTitle: Camera Based Indoor Object Detection and Distance Estimation Framework for Assistive Mobility
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel, real-time, deep learning, and computer vision-based indoor object detection and distance estimation framework for assistive mobility. Blind and visually impaired people find it difficult to deal with indoor objects and their location in their daily life. The emerging deep learning technologies can help them to do this task efficiently and conveniently by providing them with information about indoor objects present in their surroundings. In our proposed framework, we have trained the recent YOLOv7 model for indoor object detection. We have used the bounding box parameters to estimate the distance of the detected object from the user. The information on detected objects and estimated distance have been provided to visually impaired users through audio feedback. Our proposed framework will assist visually impaired people in making informed decisions and make them more confident and better prepared during their navigation in an indoor environment.

articleTitle: Intelligent Pedestrian Intention Prediction Framework
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: One of the most critical tasks in autonomous driving is anticipating pedestrian crossing intention on roads to ensure safe and reliable driving. This will instil trust in the road user community in driving assistance endeavours from Advanced Driving Assistance Systems (ADAS) to Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) encouraging their co-existence. In this paper, a cascade of three modules is employed, the convolution module that acts as a feature extractor, the recurrent module that is used for sequential tasks followed by classification module. It is shown that with the help of information regarding the past trajectory, appearance of pedestrians and the ego-vehicle speed, the proposed data-driven approach is able to predict pedestrian crossing intention reliably. The proposed algorithm is able to anticipate crossing intention in two publicly available benchmark datasets, JAAD and PIE with an accuracy of 88% and 86% respectively.

articleTitle: Propositions for Smart Healthcare Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Over the past years, chronic disease morbidity has rapidly increased. This increase has given rise to many healthcare challenges. Challenges like staff shortage, time latency in drug development, and lack of personalized attention are a few. This work aims to rank and suggest ways to mitigate different healthcare challenges. The challenges are identified through literature and ranked through Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) technique. This work Proposes the implementation of smart healthcare systems that reduce cost, increase accessibility, reduce the pressure on the healthcare worker, monitor patients' health, and store and secure medical data.

articleTitle: Robotic Electrothermal Microgripper with V-Beam Configuration for Handling Microobjects
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: In this paper, a V-shaped or chevron bent beam electrothermal microgrippers's performance is presented. Recent developments in the area of microrobotics are inextricably tied to the capacity to firmly grasp an item without causing harm to the surface or structure. The Joule heating process and thermal expansion are the theoretical foundations for the proposed chevron microgripper. It leverages the chevron form to amplify the thermal expansion in order to generate significant in-plane displacement with low power consumption. Using aluminium as a structural material and an applied electric potential of 0.2V between anchors, the behaviour of the thermal bent beam microgripper is studied. The proposed microgripper is initial closed type which produces the optimum displacement of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15.6 \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> with the 1.53GPa stress. The thermal analysis is also been done and the resultant temperature is 446°C which is less than the melting point of aluminium. The microgripper that was developed might be used for a variety of robotic tasks, including the manipulation of microobjects in the manufacturing sector, the handling of living cells, and many more.

articleTitle: Camera Based Automated Quality Assessment of Fruits for a Smart Home
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: A camera-based fruit quality system is essential for the smart home. In this work, we propose a fruit detection system based on their qualities. Sorting fruits by humans is a time-consuming process, subject to inconsistencies and influenced by surrounding conditions. In this camera-based fruit quality assessment system, the fruits are detected and predicted under qualities like Fresh and Rotten. In the system, the Camera module captures the image of the fruit and then sends it to the Quality Assessment module. In this module, the information from that image is extracted and tested based on YOLOv5. After detecting the quality, the system indicates to the the user whether the fruit is fresh or rotten. This helps the user to easily get to know about the quality of the fruit and can segregate the fruits according to their freshness. This automatic fruit handling system helps every user in a smart home to save time and buy better quality fruits.

articleTitle: Auto-Encoders for Crowd Density Estimation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Counting the number of people in an image or video has attracted the attention of several researchers due to their increasing use in situations like video monitoring, public safety, crowd control, etc. Redirecting the focus from primitive techniques like detection, regression, and clustering, this research utilizes the advanced concepts of CNNs and Computer Vision. The paper introduces a method that infers the headcount of the crowd by generating a density map using the Gaussian filter. An auto-encoder model, which is an unsupervised machine learning algorithm has been trained upon a dataset of around 1200 pictures. It comprises 4 convolutional layers for the encoder and 4 deconvolutional layers for the decoder (Conv2DTranspose). The model outperforms the cutting-edge crowd-counting methods and the mean squared error of the predicted values with respect to the test values obtained is reported to be 0.649%.

articleTitle: Prediction of Power Consumption at EV Charging Station Based on Deep Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: This paper investigates the machine learning based forecasting technique to prevent problems emerging at the electric vehicle (EV) charging station. The emergence of plug in hybrid vehicles (PHEVs) has led to certain problems like power deficit and power loss at the EV charging station. So forecasting is crucial and necessary part of an increasing number of EVs on road. In this paper, Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) technique is used to predict the power needed at the charging station beforehand. Also, the LSTM technique is compared with an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to show its efficiency and effectiveness. The effectiveness of this paper is that error is reduced significantly while predicting load at the charging station using the LSTM technique, which is much more accurate than the ANN technique applied

articleTitle: Half-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide-Based Band Stop Filter for Static Target Detection in X-Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Half-mode substrate integrated waveguide-based bandpass filter is designed for static target detection in X-band. The bandwidth of the band-stop filter (BSF) is increased by 1.5GHz i.e., the passband is from 6.5 GHz to 12 GHz. The insertion loss in the passband is 0.3 dB. When slots equivalent to a quarter wavelength are cut on the same bandpass filter, a selective BSF with passbands at 8.4, 10.4, and 12.4GHz is obtained. The target of interest can be monitored effectively when transmitted pulses encrypted with the secretive message, when correlated at the receiving side only regenerates pulses at three frequencies namely 8.4GHz, 10.4GHz, and 12.4GHz respectively. The algorithm has been written and tested successfully in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Internet of Things Based Smart Refrigeration System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Food Waste due to spoilage is a major problem in many households and restaurants. Food Waste, also known as food loss refers to food that is thrown out due to spoilage before consumed by us. The users are not warned about the freshness or expiry of their food after it has been bought and stored in a refrigerator unless they check on the goods. Furthermore, food goods are not clearly labeled with an expiry date to ensure the freshness of the food. The Internet of Things (IoT) provides a cutting-edge innovation in computing that holds the key in solving the issue. The concept of the IoT and the growth of smart kitchen appliances come together in the smart refrigeration system. There are three essential components in the system: a sensor, a controller, and a transmitter. The transmission module collaborate to analyze the food in the fridge, then sends an SMS or email to the user with updates on the perishability and amount of the food. In this paper, we present an IoT based Smart Refrigeration System to maintain proper conditions to reduce Food Wastage due to spoilage.

articleTitle: Byzantine Attack Detection in a WSN Using Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks, or WSNs, are getting employed more extensively in pandemic computing to track current status of the environment. Nevertheless, the sensors were made with a particular purpose in mind due to the severe power limitations. The extended Kalman filter algorithm is suggested in this article as a way to recognize Byzantine attacks on wireless sensor network nodes. A node is deemed to be under Byzantine attack if the difference between its expected and actual values exceeds the threshold. Then the data from that node is discarded. Additional real-time data is gathered, and simulations are run to support our assertion.

articleTitle: Logistics And Site Service Operations - A Special Focus On Green Logistics And EHS In Reactive Power Management Industry
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Organizations employ a range of business improvement initiatives to improve their operations. Supply chain management, logistics, and site services are viewed as being vital for businesses to have a competitive edge. Any organization's ability to grow depends on how well its logistics and supply chain network and planning are able to deliver goods from the factory to the site in a timely manner without sustaining any damage during transit, as well as how well its site services operations are carried out once the goods have been delivered there. However, it should also be borne in mind that the race for expansion shouldn't come at the expense of harming the environment or the well-being of the workforce, which is the growth's major asset. In this paper, site service operations, capacitor bank commissioning for reactive power management, and solutions to EHS problems during site services and logistical activities in the reactive power industry are covered in depth. To combat the effects of climate change, alternative transportation options are also proposed.

articleTitle: Texture Classification Using CNN and Dimensionality Reduction Techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Texture classification has been a popular topic in recent years for researchers. Texture classification frequently employs Convolution Neural Networks (CNN) as the traditional handcrafted methods were not successful for the immense size of data. Handcrafted methods are tedious and costly to develop and highly dependent on one application. Convolution neural networks (CNN) have recently emerged as the most important feature extractor: CNN-based feature extraction methods actually outperforms other feature extraction techniques. In precedent works, this issue of Texture Classification was resolved by deep-learning techniques but the classification accurateness was 96–97 percent. Deep learning actually learn features in incremental manner. But in CNN we deals with millions of parameters. Training it with large and complex data models can be expensive. It also needs extensive hardware. So Deep Learning has very high Dimensionality. So. in my methodology i have used Dimensionality reduction technique after the Feature extraction. So that further reduce the multidimensional to fewer dimension in Visualization. So, In my work, I have proposed the hybrid CNN technique that increases the accuracy as well as that better visualization of the network.

articleTitle: Computer Vision and Deep Learning Based Framework for Road Scene and Surface Segmentation in Unstructured Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: We propose a computer vision and deep learning-based novel framework for segmenting traffic scenes and road surface anomalies in unstructured environments. These anomalies, like potholes, water puddles, patches, etc., may cause severe accidents during driving. Information regarding the road scene and surface is essential for safe and efficient driving. The PSPNet architecture, along with EfficientNet as a backbone, has been used for segmenting road scene and surface anomalies on two different datasets, which are applicable for assessing road conditions for driving safety and road maintenance. Our proposed framework achieves benchmark performance in resource-constrained conditions using low-cost cameras and computing systems helpful in Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and Autonomous Vehicles.

articleTitle: Simulation and Investigation of Wide-Band Piezoelectric MEMS Energy Harvester for Smart Electronic Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: A major challenge that arises with the broad use of wireless smart sensor networks is the provision of energy for these wireless sensors over extended periods of time. Energy harvesting is a rapidly expanding industry, and researchers and developers are making steady progress in optimizing power output from existing sources. Solar, wind, thermal, vibrational, and other forms of energy are only some of the ad hoc options that may be found in nature. In comparison to the other approaches, energy harvesting using vibrational energy sources stands out for its independence from external factors and its universal availability. Due to its great effectiveness in converting ambient vibration into usable energy and its relatively simple design, piezoelectric energy harvesters have become the subject of much study. Here, we propose utilizing COMSOL Multiphysics Software to build, simulate, and analyze a micro-cantilever array-based piezoelectric energy harvester. An array of cantilevers of varying lengths is created to harvest energy from a broad spectrum of vibrational force. Using EB beam theory, the ideal proportions of length to breadth and length to depth are determined. The suggested energy harvester can produce a maximum voltage of 0.6 V with a resistive load of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1000\ \Omega$</tex> and an input acceleration of 1; this may be adjusted for our specific areas of study and practical applications. Collectively, a huge array of these cantilever beams might provide a higher voltage that could be utilized to power smart electronic devices.

articleTitle: 5 and L Shaped ACS Fed MIMO Antenna with Improved Isolation and Diversity Metrics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: An antenna having the ability of operating in 2.19GHz – 2.38 GHz, 3.37GHz – 3.65 GHz and 4.73GHz – 6.69 GHz bandwidths is recommended in this paper. The capability of the designed antenna is attained using 5 and L shape. This MIMO antenna is designed with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$53\times 53\times 1.6\ mm^{3}$</tex> configuration to control the capacity of the system. The interference and impedance matching of the system is controlled by the orthogonal positioning of elements and it is presented as return loss graph with a value ¡−15 dB. The results section presents the designed antenna performance in the graphs of gain, efficiency and radiation patterns. For the detailed control of antenna the diversity metrics like ECC, MEG, CCL, TARC and DG are presented with graphs having acceptable ranges.

articleTitle: Tree Branch Shaped Triple Band ACS Fed MIMO Antenna for High Speed Data Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: For improved isolation and high data rates a 4 element Tree branch shaped MIMO Antenna is designed in a triple frequency band producing good bandwidth within the ranges is described in this article. A tree branch shaped ACS fed antenna operating in frequency ranges 2.22–2.42GHz, 3.28–3.43GHz and 4.52–7.27GHz is a portable antenna which can be used for WiMAX, WLAN, WiMAX applications. This antenna is designed based on spatial multiplexing concept to increase the data carrying capacity of channel without the requirement of additional bandwidth. The diversity parameters ECC, DG, MEG, TARC and CCL are mentioned in this article and radiation patterns which are bidirectional and nearly omnidirectional are also mentioned at different frequencies in operating bands.

articleTitle: Cloud Classification Method Based on Convolutional Encoder and Multimodal Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: To overcome the challenges posed by the lack of uniqueness, limited categories, and inaccurate representations of clouds, this paper has presented a cloud classification method based on convolutional encoder and multimodal feature fusion. Firstly, to extract the most representative cloud features, we designed a Cloud-SSAE model, which adds a convolution neural network on top of the autoencoder learning mechanism, incorporates a penalty term within the hidden layer to promote sparsity in the subsequent input layer, and utilizes max-pooling to increase the robustness of the features. Secondly, we improved VGG16 model by incorporating dilated convolution to obtain dense local features. We further fused the color, texture, morphology, temperature, and humidity into the multimodal features. Lastly, we combined Cloud-SSAE model features, VGG16 model features, and multimodal features, and input the fused features into Support vector machine for classification. Consequently, the method proposed herein has the capacity to facilitate the classification of 11 distinct cloud types, encompassing but not restricted to cirrus and cumulonimbus cloud, with an improved accuracy level of 92.1%.

articleTitle: Exploring the Role of Conventional and Non-Conventional Technologies in Identifying MDD
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: The most prevalent mental health condition is known as major depressive disorder (MDD), which is characterized by low mood, loss of interest, anxiety as well as hopelessness, cognitive decline, and even suicidal ideation. By 2020, depression is expected to surpass all other disorders in terms of medical burden and functional impairment at work, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Unfortunately, the characteristics of depression vary, making an accurate and timely diagnosis challenging. To diagnose MDD, both conventional and non-conventional methods are frequently used. Conventional methods that use brain waves to detect depression include electroencephalography (EEG) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), among others. Non-conventional methods include text, audio, and image-based. However, a significant amount of cutting-edge research is being done to develop additional possible tools and technologies by fusing other algorithms with ML/DL algorithms, as this provides a variety of unique applications and opens the door to more research.

articleTitle: Leveraging Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Understanding the Effect of Model Capacity on Training Dataset Size
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Automated Image classification has seen substantial growth in recent times. However, several applications suffer from the limited availability of training data, such as the classification of medical images, where data collection is mostly limited by privacy concerns of human subjects. As a result, to compensate for the limited availability of training data, most of these applications employ custom-made lightweight architectures. While state-of-the-art deep models for computer vision applications usually exploit architectures with huge model capacity. However, the increase in model complexity and size necessarily doesn't guarantee better performance on small medical datasets. We study this phenomenon in the context of medical images, where several existing studies report that most sophisticated deep networks for computer vision trained on large datasets such as Image Net do not generalize on medical image applications, due to huge model capacity, subsequently leading to overfitting on smaller training datasets. In this research, we exploit explainable artificial intelligence to analyze the features learned by state-of-the-art deep models for smaller medical image training datasets and contrast them with the features learned for larger medical training datasets. In particular, we exploit Shapley Additive explanations (SHAP) features to perform a qualitative comparison of feature relevance maps and understand how different standard models when trained with different training sizes understand discriminative image patterns to perform classification. Furthermore, we also compare SHAP features on scenarios in which the same model focuses on images belonging to different classes. Experiments on two datasets of different sizes have been presented to understand the dependence of model complexity on the number of samples in the training dataset. Results demonstrate that simpler models learn generalizable SHAP features that allow them to perform better on small datasets, unlike larger models when trained on smaller datasets. Likewise, bigger models when trained on larger datasets learn more distinctive and diverse features that allow them to outperform smaller models.

articleTitle: A Greedy Task Allocation Mechanism for Time-Dependent Mobile Crowdsensing Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Task allocation is the process that facilitates the assignment of sensing activities or tasks to participants of a Mobile Crowdsensing (MCS) campaign. In traditional MCS environments, the purpose of task allocation is to maximize the profit of the organizing platform. However, the task allocation approach in these systems fail to deal with the specifics of time-dependent nature of the tasks and the issues that accompany time-dependent task allocation. Hence, we propose a novel mechanism called Time Dependent Task Allocation (TDTA) to allocate tasks in order to achieve maximum profit of the platform in a truly time-dependent mobile crowdsensing environment. In order to realize our goal, we also propose an algorithm for handling time-dependent task allocation called Interval Partition based Greedy Task Allocation (IPGTA). We then compare our proposed IPGTA algorithm with a baseline method and analyze their comparative performances. The simulation results indicate that IPGTA performs positively based on the parameters measured.

articleTitle: Interlinking Farm Produce and Stakeholders Through QGIS Maps in Madurai
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: For a developing country like India, agriculture is the backbone of its economy. Nevertheless, farmers face significant challenges all year long. Overproduction is a common problem among farmers. There might be regions in the city deprived of harvest while somewhere the crop is redundant. The study area selected is the district of Madurai in the state of Tamil Nadu, India with a cultural richness and devotion to agriculture and also a hot spot for tourism. Thus, our main aim is to provide maps of location of farm lands, hotels, catering services and food processing industries in our study area. With this GIS – based information system assisted data analysis, a network of various agricultural sectors can be connected directly without any middleman in order to reduce wastage and promote the farmer's well-being thereby benefitting farmers and the community in every aspect.

articleTitle: Diagnosis and Classification of Cancer Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: There are many types of cancers that are dangerous for human beings. Especially Breast cancer is one of the most common reasons for increasing death in women worldwide. Diagnosis of breast cancer at the initial stage can minimize the mortality rate significantly. It is possible using machine learning algorithms. A cancer patient can survive longer if the model is more accurate and precise. A smart framework is essential to detect and classify breast cancer at an early stage with high accuracy and precision. In this study, a model is implemented using machine learning techniques for the detection and classification of breast cancer. We have used a support vector classifier (SVC), Naive Bayes, logistic regression, and k-nearest neighbor algorithms for classification purposes. After obtaining results, model performance is analyzed based on different evaluation matrices. Sensitivity, selectivity, accuracy, precision, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f1$</tex>-score is taken into consideration as the performance measures. It is detected that the support vector classifier accomplished the maximum accuracy (98%), precision, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f1$</tex>-score. Python programming language and Scikit-learn library are used for this work.

articleTitle: Pedestrian Trajectory Forecasting in Videos
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Pedestrian trajectory forecasting is an important research problem in computer vision, especially in autonomous vehicles and autonomous mobile robots. Now-a-days, from augmented reality to simulation, from small mobile robots to self-driving cars, human motion modeling has become an active research area. Pedestrian trajectory forecasting can be seen as part of human motion modeling, where based on the past behaviour, one tries to predict what might be the future path. In this paper, we attempt to address this problem. We create a dataset and propose a pedestrian trajectory forecasting pipeline that senses the environment, detects and tracks pedestrians and forecasts the future trajectory of the pedestrians in the video. We propose an LSTM-based motion model to forecast the sequential information of the pedestrians for the next few frames. Our LSTM-based motion forecasting model is trained and tested on custom annotated surveillance datasets. Our experimental results show that our proposed framework is robust and accurate.

articleTitle: Content Based Movie Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: A recommendation system is a system that suggests resources to the user like books, movies, song, etc. based on some dataset. A movie recommender system usually generates opinion about what the user would like to view, but it is always a cumbersome task to select a movie because the dataset of movies around the world is large. Although, this issue can be resolved with the help of a movie Recommendation System (RS), which uses content-based filtering. This RS recommends movies to the users based on the content they are searching and watching. In this article, a dataset from Kaggle is used for the implementation of content-based filtering using machine learning (cosine similarities) with vectorization and the data analysis tool used is Python.

articleTitle: Predicting Bitcoin Trends Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Algorithms via Continuous and Binary Data — A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Bitcoin is a cutting-edge payment system and a brand-new form of money known as a cryptocurrency. A cryptocurrency is a digital asset designed with the purpose of securing financial transactions, preventing the creation of new units, and validating the transfer of assets. It uses strong cryptography to do these things. Because we can't predict accurately and sentiment analysis of bitcoin from twitter tweets, we seek to utilize machine learning to examine historical changes in currency prices and try to discern a trend in prices. A competent chart reading talent can assist you in determining whether to purchase or sell. The project we are working on demonstrates or assists you in determining when to purchase or sell any stock. Our program collects data from the previous years. As the software accumulates data over a longer period of time, its accuracy improves. After gathering the data, it creates its own chart by evaluating prior occurrences, and that chart can assist in determining when to purchase and when to sell. This analysis is tested using various machine learning and deep learning algorithms. As predicted Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) have dominated in results compared to the other models used for prediction.

articleTitle: Automated Evaluation Approach for Time-Dependent QA Pairs on Web Crawler-Based QA System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to deal with the generalized Question Answering (QA) system. This work demonstrates an end to end system that is capable of dealing with the open domain questions i.e. not particular to any genre. For this research different technologies like beautiful Soup is used to scrape the web, MS-Marco dataset is used to train and shorten the document using transfer learning. Document/answers obtained using these processes are validated using an exact match with the Gold answer available in the dataset. This automatic evaluation method fails due to linguistic ambiguities inherent in the data. Taking limitation of this automatic evaluation method as a challenge, in this work an heuristic approach is proposed to deal with the Questions and answers that are dependent on time. A metric is proposed that uses current timestamp and top-n predicted answers from QA system as input. This approach is further tested on the publicly available GNQ(Google Natural Question) dataset. Out of that we have tested for 100 odd pairs and achieved an accuracy of 78% for the test data. The proposed heuristic approach appears to have the great prospect of developing into a beneficial scheme for gathering pinpoint, credible, and specific information in an accurate, real-time and efficient manner.

articleTitle: Welcome Message
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: We extend a warm and heartfelt welcome to the 16th IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI 2022), hosted virtually from 2nd – 4th December 2022, in the vibrant city of Delhi, India. As the General Chairs of this remarkable gathering, we are delighted to convey our greetings to all of you who have joined us for this intellectually enriching and collaborative event.

articleTitle: Dispensation of the Sum of Shadowed-Rician RV's and Applications in Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: The dispensation for addition of two random variables (R.V.) performs a crucial role for the evaluation of range techniques for wireless communication technology as compared to fading channels even as for common fading fashions which include the Rician fading, Rayleigh fading and Nakagamim fading. The diversity technique can be understand by the Shadowed-Rician (SR) with alter Line of Sight (LOS) issuance. We investigate the channel model with the help of sum of two SR RVs. We are using the general process of the RV so we can generalize this case to many sample cases about RV's instead of a single one. In this paper, the derivation of probability density function (p.d.f.) and cumulative distribution function (c.d.f.) has been done using the gamma functions for analyzing the satellite communication systems.

articleTitle: Chatbot for Healthcare System Using NLP and Python
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: After the 20th century ended, people in the 21st century started to worry more about their own health and the health of their families. Realizing that “health is wealth,” they decide that their health is the one asset they should safeguard throughout their lives. It is significant that medication is essentially necessary for most individuals to lead happy lives. However, it may be challenging to schedule an appointment with a doctor for every issue that arises in our bodies. The goal is to use Python and JSON to build a healthcare bot that, prior contacting a physician, could recognize the illness and give accurate, basic information about that as well. This will essentially contribute to lowering healthcare expenses and expanding access to health records through a healthcare chatbot, both of which are very important. These AI systems were software applications which utilise Python as a driver and will basically be kept in a CV file to basically communicate with users, proving that this will basically help to cut medical expenses and enhance accessibility to medical information through medical chatbots, or so they think. The idea is to primarily use Python and JSON to create a clinical bots which can recognise a illness and often offer additional basic details well about disorder prior to actually visiting a physician. The bots warehouses the database's information in order to recognise the statement keyword phrases, to start making a query judgement, and to respond to the query. This again illustrates how well the concept essentially is to generate a healthcare chatbot. Through offering appropriate advice on healthy lifestyle, a healthcare Chatbot can help resolve this issue. Natural language processing underpins its operation of healthcare chatbots and enables users to communicate health-related problems.

articleTitle: Mapping Vulnerabilities of Indian Long-Haul Truck Drivers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: To understand the occupational and socio-economic vulnerabilities experienced by truck drivers, one hundred nine long-haul truck drivers employed under truck-fleet owners of Delhi NCR were surveyed through a questionnaire. Participants were recruited as per convenience and snowball methods of sampling. The questionnaire was administered verbally in Hindi, transcribed, and subjected to descriptive analysis. Results indicate trucking sector in India is unorganised, with little to no standardisation in terms of the compensation rate for driving labour. While drivers receive meagre pay for long work hours, they are exposed to health difficulties and frequently engage in unsafe practices such as over-speeding. Indian truck drivers are burdened with various financial and social disadvantages due to the unorganised nature of the trucking sector. Drivers are compensated only for driving labour, and other costs related to their health and well-being are mostly externalised from the supply chain, negatively impacting their quality of life. A recommended future direction is to direct research towards reorganising this sector by restructuring the industry practice of incentivising faster delivery time, standardising terms of employment for truck drivers, and upskilling them through vocational training.

articleTitle: Automation in Hydroponic Systems: A Sustainable Pathway to Modern Farming
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Researchers are searching for different ways to enhance agricultural productivity since the human population is growing at an exponential rate. Additionally, rural-urban immigration has resulted in an overpopulation of the cities and a lack of farmers on the farms in the rural areas. In hydroponic farming, crops are produced without the use of soil. By using this method, the fields may follow the farmers into the city. Automation is the hydroponics industry's last frontier. One farmer will be able to manage many farms at once and work multiple jobs. Farmers can now monitor every variable influences the plant growth under hydroponics because of automation. This study concludes literature in the design of different types of hydroponics systems. The type of automation in hydroponic system based on microcontrollers, the role of various monitoring variables in automated hydroponics and the type of automation used for an intelligent hydroponic system are part of discussion. The above mentioned developments will raise hydroponics' productivity and potential for the hydroponics market in the near future.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient MAC Framework Under Temporal Fading in WBAN
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: Wireless Body Area Networks (WBANs) have piqued the curiosity of many programmers and academics due to recent developments of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). WBAN is a network of small, light in weight, efficient in energy that track population well being for early detection and treatment. Biomedical Sensor Nodes are powered by connected batteries, which are an important feature of their design. Furthermore, the restricted battery capacity limitation is linked to a worry about how to lower node energy usage to prolong lifespan of the network. As a consequence the IEEE 802.15.6 low-power WBAN standard that enables wireless communication within or close a human body is popular. To solve the challenges and requirements of WBAN, this standard created additional PHY and MAC layers. In this work the Medium Access Control (MAC) IEEE 802.15.6 is explored in terms of scheduled Vs contention based channel access schemes. As the human body has postural mobility, which causes distance variations and changes in the status of BMSNs connections over time. So, we compare IEEE-802.15.6 in GTS mode (Guaranteed time slot) with CSMA/CA mode (Carrier Sense Multiple Access) under postural mobility of human in WBAN. The simulation results are done by varying the RAP (Random Access Period) phase, to show the performance evaluations in terms of packet received by Head of Nodes (HoN) and application level latency by comparing the Temporal VS noTemporal variations.

articleTitle: Multi Objective Generation Dispatch for Bulky Thermal Power Plants Using Novel Corona Virus Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel bio-inspired meta-heuristics (BIM) imposing highest quality scheduling for price of fuel for generating devices and emission level for cumbersome thermal devices subjected to valve factor loading, ramp rate constraints, ice deposition, wind strain and, prohibited running zones in addition to equality and inequality constraints. When compared to certain other comparable tactics, this corona virus (CV) optimization algorithm (CVOA) has two key advantages. To begin with, entered parameters are pre-determined based on disease data, prohibiting researchers from starting with random values. Second, techniques, in addition to putting this pace, have the ability to stop after a certain number of iterations. A virus variant is also proposed, in which multiple corona virus trails evolve in parallel and investigate a larger search area in a smaller number of epochs. Finally, heuristic algorithms and deep learning have been merged to know (DL) models, to discover most effective hyper-parameters at some stage in the education phase. Using a concurrent multi virus variant, where many corona virus lines evolve simultaneously and cover a larger search region in fewer iterations. Ultimate scheduling is carried out for three extraordinary test cases involving aforesaid constraints and it is ascertained that the results obtained outperform different soft computing (SC) methods.

Author Keywords: acute severe chronic respiratory coronavirus 2 optimization

articleTitle: Camera Based Framework for Collision Avoidance in Intelligent Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (SOLI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a framework for collision avoidance with respect to Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and Intelligent Vehicles (IV). We extract monocular 3D information of road environment and utilize it to assess a threat level for developing a collision avoidance system for ADAS and IV. The input frames are captured by a dashcam mounted on the dashboard of a vehicle. First, the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model is trained to provide dimensions of objects, orientation of objects, keypoints and rectangular detection box around the object. Keypoint and orientation provides 3D bounding boxes with given camera calibration matrix and ground plane. For more accurate 3D boxes, selection of ground plane is done based on a polling method. Moreover, the objects are tracked using a deep learning based approach and their relative speed is calculated based on the relative movement of 3D boxes surrounding the object. Orientation and location of object with respect to the camera provides the direction of movement. The estimated direction and relative speed are then combined to discover the threat level for collision which is depicted in the incoming frames based on colored bounding boxes of the objects of interest. These color levels, namely, Red, Orange, Yellow, Green and Blue are based decreasing threat levels of objects. This provides accurate information regarding the degree of threat for potential collision with the objects of interest in the environment. Experimental results show that our framework is robust and provides important information for collision avoidance.
